entries.sense_en: torn, ragged pieces of cloth; worn-out clothing

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for old, worn cloth or clothes; does not stress that they are torn apart.
Thin, torn strips; stresses that something has been ripped up.

entries.sense_en: padded or lined with soft stuffing for warmth

synonyms.nuance: General word for any soft filling, not only for warmth.
Stitched in layers with filling, usually in a pattern.

entries.sense_en: costing a lot of money; expensive

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word for a high price.
More formal; often suggests a serious cost or loss.
Informal and slightly critical.

entries.sense_en: promising to pay later instead of paying at once

synonyms.nuance: Business term: the buyer has an account and settles it later.
British slang for buying now and paying later.

entries.sense_en: be free to choose whichever you like

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; offers a choice without stressing how many options there are.

entries.sense_en: to attach a new leather bottom to a shoe or boot

synonyms.nuance: Same job, but stresses that a worn sole is being replaced.
Much wider: fix any damage, not only the bottom.

entries.sense_en: walked slowly and heavily, as if tired

synonyms.nuance: Slow, steady, dull walking; also used for slow, dull work.

Relaxed, pleasant walking; the opposite feeling to trudge.

entries.sense_en: to be worried or unhappy about something

synonyms.nuance: Most common; a general word for anxious thoughts.
Think about a problem silently and gloomily for a long time.
Informal: stay upset about something without acting.

entries.sense_en: have drunk a little alcohol

synonyms.nuance: Old-fashioned and light; a small habitual drink.
A quick small drink of strong liquor.

entries.sense_en: having very little money

synonyms.nuance: Informal; has no money at the moment.
Neutral; a temporary lack of money.
Complete lack of money; stronger and more literary.

entries.sense_en: to pay money, usually unwillingly

synonyms.nuance: Very close; also informal and implies reluctance.
Informal; pay when pressed or forced.
Pay a debt that is due; not necessarily unwillingly.

entries.sense_en: a small holy place by the road where people pray

The table for religious offerings inside a church or temple, not the whole place.
The holiest part of a temple; also a place of safe refuge.

entries.sense_en: looked hard because it was difficult to see

synonyms.nuance: Half-close the eyes, usually because of bright light or weak eyesight.
Look for a long time, usually with the eyes wide open.
Look steadily, often with wonder or love.

entries.sense_en: to see or understand something with difficulty

synonyms.nuance: Formal; see or notice something faint or subtle.
synonyms.example: discern a shape in the fog

synonyms.nuance: Tell one thing from another by seeing differences.

entries.tip_ko: 'make out'은 문맥에 따라 '이해하다/알아보다/(그럴듯하게) 주장하다'로 뜻이 달라진다.

entries.sense_en: to get involved in something that is not your business

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; get in the way or change things you should not.
Ask or look into private matters out of curiosity.
Touch or change something, often causing harm.

entries.sense_en: to hold someone's throat tight to stop their breathing

synonyms.nuance: Stronger and more common; suggests killing by squeezing the neck.
Can also mean to have trouble breathing yourself.

entries.sense_en: made him feel sudden guilt (his conscience troubled him strongly)

synonyms.nuance: Milder; a small, sharp pang of guilt.
General; make someone uneasy.

entries.sense_en: the inner sense of right and wrong

synonyms.nuance: Doubts that stop you from doing something wrong; usually plural.
Beliefs about right and wrong; more about principles than feeling.

entries.sense_en: having a pleasing, well-formed shape

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; the parts are properly and neatly shaped.

entries.sense_en: falling behind and failing to keep up

synonyms.nuance: Fall behind in a loose, untidy way, often in a group.

entries.sense_en: a special skill for doing something easily

synonyms.nuance: A clever method learned by experience; can be taught quickly.

Natural style and stylish ability.

entries.tip_ko: 첫 발음 k는 소리 나지 않는다: [낵].

entries.sense_en: sad and without hope after a disappointment

synonyms.nuance: Stronger, more formal; deeply low in spirits.

A general dark mood, not necessarily caused by a setback.

entries.sense_en: a sour Russian drink made from fermented bread

entries.sense_en: breathing noisily through the nose because of cold

Sniffle while crying or complaining; disapproving.

entries.sense_en: the slightly drunk, light-headed state after a little alcohol

synonyms.nuance: Stronger; being really drunk.
Formal or legal word for being under the effect of alcohol.

entries.sense_en: to deceive someone

synonyms.nuance: General; make someone believe something false.
Formal; trick someone who is easy to cheat.
Informal; cheat by winning trust first.

entries.sense_en: out enjoying oneself and spending money, especially on drink

synonyms.nuance: Stronger; too much drinking or eating.
Out for a night of entertainment; not necessarily excess.

entries.sense_en: useless and lazy; of no worth

synonyms.nuance: Simply has no value; not especially about laziness.
Unwilling to work; less insulting.
Old-fashioned noun for an idle, failed person.

entries.sense_en: a dishonest person; someone who cannot be trusted

synonyms.nuance: Stronger; a wicked, dishonest man.

Modern, informal word for a criminal.

entries.sense_en: to talk too much or gossip

synonyms.nuance: Talk about other people's private lives.
Talk quickly and continuously about unimportant things.

entries.sense_en: a homeless person who wanders from place to place

synonyms.nuance: Legal, official word; often connected with begging.
British; a homeless person who walks the roads.
A person who moves around without a settled job or home.

entries.sense_en: to behave cruelly toward someone

synonyms.nuance: Nearly the same; the usual modern word.

entries.sense_en: with the eyebrows drawn together, showing pain or worry

synonyms.nuance: Stresses the lines in the forehead.
Everyday word for a displeased look.

entries.sense_en: to talk very fast and without stopping

synonyms.nuance: Fast talk about minor things.
Talk on and on, often boringly.
American idiom with the same idea.

entries.tip_ko: 영국식 관용구로 '시끄럽게 쉼 없이' 말하는 모습을 나타낸다.

entries.sense_en: the stitched joins split open

synonyms.nuance: Come apart along a line, often lengthwise.

entries.sense_en: to die, especially from cold, hunger or disaster

synonyms.nuance: The plain, everyday word.
Give in to an illness or hardship and die.
Formal; cease to live, or (of documents) run out.

entries.sense_en: stiff and rigid, as a dead body is

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; hard to bend, including a body after death.
Completely unable to bend; more formal.

entries.tip_ko: 'stark naked'(홀딱 벗은)처럼 부사로 '완전히'를 뜻하기도 하지만, 여기서는 시신이 굳었다는 뜻의 형용사다.

entries.sense_en: prepared a dead body for burial

synonyms.nuance: General; get something ready.
Put clothes on the body for the funeral.

entries.sense_en: cutting down (a tree)

synonyms.nuance: Everyday; cut with an axe.
Neutral; by any tool.
Cut trees for timber as a trade.

entries.sense_en: flowed over the edge because there was too much

Be full to the edge without spilling.

entries.sense_en: became successful and wealthy

Reach a goal; not always about money.

entries.sense_en: the horizontal beam above a door

synonyms.nuance: The whole frame around a door.
Any long support piece of wood or metal.

entries.sense_en: big, broad and strong

synonyms.nuance: Short and solid.
Shows strong muscles, whatever the size.
Informal; heavy and strong, sometimes fat.

entries.sense_en: breathed out heavily, tired from effort or annoyed

synonyms.nuance: Breathe fast with the mouth open after running.
Breathe out loudly to show annoyance.

entries.sense_en: bent the head and body forward and down

synonyms.nuance: General word to curve the body.
Lower the head quickly to avoid something.
Bend the knees to sit low; closer to the ground.

entries.sense_en: shouted in a loud, angry voice

Loud and deep, like a bull.
Quick, sharp and irritated, but not necessarily loud.

entries.sense_en: looking steadily for a long time

synonyms.nuance: Fixed look, often rude or shocked.
Very quick look.
Stare with the mouth open in surprise.

entries.sense_en: moved with a small quick jerk

synonyms.nuance: One sharp movement; often stronger.
Smooth, playful movement side to side.
Move back suddenly from pain or fear.

entries.sense_en: the upper front part of a boot or shoe

The hard covering at the toe end.

entries.sense_en: quicker and more skilful in movement

synonyms.nuance: Moves easily and gracefully, e.g. an athlete.
Skilful with the hands; neat and sure.
Simple speed, without the skill.

entries.sense_en: (of a shoe) having a strip of leather sewn between upper and sole

synonyms.nuance: Sewn with thread, in any way.
Strengthened by adding extra material.

entries.sense_en: to speak sharply to someone for a fault

synonyms.nuance: Everyday; usually to children.
Formal; official criticism by an authority.
Long, angry criticism.

entries.sense_en: to get down from a vehicle

synonyms.nuance: Everyday; leave a bus, train or bike.
Leave a ship, plane or train; formal.
Get off a horse or bicycle.

entries.sense_en: small pieces left over after the main part is used

synonyms.nuance: Small useless bits, often thrown away.
Mostly food remaining after a meal.
Neutral; whatever is left, often of something destroyed.

entries.sense_en: an uneven way of walking because of an injured leg

synonyms.nuance: Walk with difficulty and pain, taking small steps.
Walk unsteadily as if about to fall, e.g. when drunk.

entries.sense_en: a small catch that holds a door shut

synonyms.nuance: A sliding metal bar; stronger.
General word for a small fastener.

entries.sense_en: a square cloth worn over the head or neck

synonyms.nuance: Longer, usually worn around the neck for warmth.
Cotton square, patterned; worn on head or neck.
Specifically covers the head.

entries.sense_en: listened and gave in to a request

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word for paying attention to sounds.
Pay attention to advice or warning and act on it.

entries.sense_en: hung down and became limp

synonyms.nuance: Sink down in the middle.
Lose strength; mostly plants.

entries.sense_en: weakly, with little strength

synonyms.nuance: Plain, neutral word for lacking strength.
Barely noticeable, in sound or sight.

entries.sense_en: forgave and removed the punishment

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and personal; stop being angry.
Overlook a small fault.
Formally free from guilt or blame.

entries.sense_en: extremely hungry

synonyms.nuance: Very hungry (often used loosely in speech).
Hungry enough to eat greedily.

entries.sense_en: a very bad smell

synonyms.nuance: Common, less formal word for a bad smell.

Neutral; a smell, good or bad.

entries.sense_en: a feeling of great respect mixed with fear and wonder

synonyms.nuance: Amazed pleasure at something beautiful or new.
Deep respect, without fear.
Great fear; no admiration.

entries.sense_en: lost all hope

synonyms.nuance: Idiom; give up because of a setback.
Stop trying, not always with strong feeling.

entries.sense_en: a close companion who shares work or hardship

synonyms.nuance: A person who spends time with you.
British and informal.
Someone who supports you in a struggle.

entries.sense_en: begged earnestly

synonyms.nuance: Everyday, direct word.
Formal and emotional.
Beg with strong emotion or reasons.

entries.sense_en: uncovered; showed what had been hidden

synonyms.nuance: Show something usually covered or hidden.
Make known or visible, often surprisingly.
Take the cover off.

entries.sense_en: to recover one's senses after shock or a trance

synonyms.nuance: British; wake up after fainting.
Formal and medical.
Informal; stop being in a daze.
